images.title: The division method
images.purpose: Show the division method layout: a prime divisor on the left, the quotient carried down, stopping at a prime.
images.composition: One division ladder sits slightly left of centre with large digits; a single result line sits to its right with plenty of white space around both.
exact_structure: A ladder of exactly 3 rows with a vertical grey #6B7280 bar between the divisor column and the number column, and a short horizontal grey line under each of the first 2 rows.
Row 1: divisor 3 (teal #0072B2) on the left of the bar, number 105 on the right.
Row 2: divisor 5 (teal #0072B2) on the left of the bar, number 35 on the right.
Row 3: no divisor; number 7 on the right, circled in reddish purple #CC79A7 to show it is prime, the stop point, with the small reddish purple note Stop at a prime beside the circle.
A thin amber #E69F00 arrow curves from the divisor column and the final 7 to the result line on the right: 105 = 3 × 5 × 7.
rejection: any row whose divisor times the number below does not equal the number above (3 × 35 = 105, 5 × 7 = 35)
more or fewer than 3 rows in the ladder
a composite number written as a divisor
images.takeaway: Divide by a prime each time, carry the quotient down, and stop when the number left is prime.
images.description: A division ladder for 105: 3 beside 105, 5 beside 35, then 7 circled, giving 105 = 3 × 5 × 7.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on factor trees and the division method.
images.teaching_notes: Read down the left column and add the last number at the bottom to collect the primes.

image_decisions.why: The division ladder is a layout students must see to copy correctly.
